candidates.tagline: Meta's big AI hardware vision: a keychain Tamagotchi, shipping maybe in December
candidates.story: On September 23, 2026, Mark Zuckerberg unveiled the Muse Charm — a palm-sized keychain device with a tiny screen and fingerprint sensor for talking to Meta's Muse AI agent — which reviewers immediately compared to a 1990s Tamagotchi; the components aren't even finalised yet, and it won't ship until the holidays.
candidates.why_funny: Meta's answer to 'what replaces the smartphone?' is a keychain you press to ask your AI something, and Zuckerberg announced it at a splashy event while admitting the components aren't done yet.
candidates.alt: Mark Zuckerberg presenting the Meta Muse Charm — a small palm-sized device with a tiny screen — at the Meta Connect announcement event in September 2026

candidates.tagline: Galway spent €28,000 on a new logo. It looks identical to a Belgian shelf company.
candidates.story: Galway City Council unveiled a new lowercase 'g' logo on September 17, 2026 as part of a €28,000 'brand evolution' — only for the public to discover it is nearly identical to the logo of Gondella, a Belgian retail shelving company, as well as two other European brands; the Labour councillor said 'They've made a balls of it.'
candidates.why_funny: The city paid a designer €28,000 to replace a beloved 40-year-old logo with one indistinguishable from a warehouse-fitting company, sparking a grassroots campaign where locals changed their profile photos to preserve the old design.
candidates.alt: Irish publican Fergus McGinn standing in his McGinn's Hop House bar in Galway beside the beloved old Galway City Council 'G' logo — the 1980s design that the council's €28,000 rebrand replaced
